author: agent
text:
Re-read after 0.54.2. The correction recorded below still holds - the docstring no longer claims body-hash stamping, which was false after stamping unified on stamp_for.

What changed: this passes repo_root to stamp_for now, so the MCP write path stamps against the WORKING TREE like the CLI and console paths do. All three still route through the single stamp_for; the argument is the only difference, and that is the point - the drift this function's own history records (CLI stamping body_hash while agent_meta stamped logic_hash) came from two implementations, not two arguments.

Consequence worth knowing at this coordinate: an agent that edits code and then writes a note NO LONGER has to re-index first for the note to be fresh. Before 0.54.2 the note carried the pre-edit hash and was stale the moment the index caught up, which made the supersede-what-you-staled rule unable to do its job even when followed exactly.

If the ref has vanished from the working tree, stamp_for raises GhostEntity and this surface should let it become a clear error rather than writing a note that can never be fresh.
